notes.text: Mishnah 3:8 appears in the Bavli at 19a. The story also occurs in a baraita at 23a. The Yerushalmi passage numbered 3:9:4 in the cited edition identifies Yudan Girya where Heilprin has Yudan Mari.

Maharsha cites Yefeh Mareh for the distinction between the two Chonis and then offers a harmonization of the Bavli with the Yuchasin account. Heilprin supplies the numbered dates and later gives his own proposal while retaining his stated difficulty. The two Talmud narratives and the death tradition remain separate.

Patz’s translation of Yosippon records the besiegers finding and killing Choni. Josephus is a separate earlier parallel. Shalshelet’s later notice reports the claimed identification with Pinchas ben Yair and its author’s failed search for the passage in the Zohar.

The mystical reports remain attributed to Gilgulei Neshamot. The mediated Galilot witness has Par’am. The Warsaw witness gives Paniam and also reports competing burial locators. Those locators remain qualified.
